Their full bloom against the backdrop of the five-story pagoda is a truly superb farewell view of spring in Kyoto.
quiz_en: On the grounds of which temple do the short Omuro cherry trees, whose blossoms open at eye level, bloom?

desc_en: This palace was the residence of successive emperors until the capital moved to Tokyo with the Meiji Restoration. Located within the vast Kyoto Gyoen, it contains buildings such as the Shishinden, where enthronement ceremonies were held, and the Seiryoden, the emperor's everyday residence. Today it is open to the public year-round, and you can tour a space that conveys the elegance of imperial court culture.
quiz_en: What is the main hall of the Kyoto Imperial Palace, where important ceremonies such as imperial enthronements were held, called?

desc_en: Located within the Kyoto Gyoen, this garden was built as the palace of retired emperors. Most of the buildings were lost to fire, but the pond-stroll garden said to have been designed by Kobori Enshu remains. The round stones laid across the pond's pebble beach are beautiful, and you can stroll through an elegant garden where the nature of each season blends in perfect harmony.
quiz_en: The round stones on the beach of the Sento Imperial Palace are said to have been traded one each for a sho of rice, so what are they called?

desc_en: Rooted in the food served at tea ceremonies, this is Kyoto's traditional multi-course cuisine. It makes the most of seasonal ingredients and expresses the season through tableware and presentation, and its appeal lies in delicate flavors that bring out the umami of dashi (broth). Enjoyed in a tatami room of a ryotei (traditional restaurant) while gazing at the garden, it lets you feel the spirit of Kyoto hospitality.
quiz_en: The word "kaiseki" comes from Zen monks putting what inside the fold of their robes to stave off hunger?

name_en: Kyoto Cuisine on Riverside Dining Platforms
desc_en: A summer tradition in Kyoto, this is Kyoto cuisine enjoyed on platforms built over or beside a river. Along the Kamo River, the "noryo-yuka" extend from restaurant rooms over the riverbank, while in Kibune in the northern part of the city, the "kawadoko" are set up above the mountain stream. You can enjoy summer Kyoto dishes such as hamo (pike conger) while feeling the murmur of the river and the cool breeze.
quiz_en: If you dined on a riverside platform in summer Kyoto, would you choose the Kamo River in town or the mountain stream at Kibune, and why?

desc_en: Located at the foot of the Higashiyama hills in Sakyo Ward, Kyoto, this is the head temple of the Nanzen-ji branch of Rinzai Zen. Its massive Sanmon gate is known from the kabuki scene in which Ishikawa Goemon strikes a pose and exclaims, "What a superb view!" On the grounds stands the Suirokaku aqueduct of the Lake Biwa Canal, built in the Meiji era, and its unique scenery of brick arches harmonizing with the old temple is popular.
quiz_en: In kabuki, which great thief strikes a pose atop the Sanmon gate of Nanzen-ji and exclaims, "What a superb view!"?

desc_en: This old temple stands halfway up Mount Kurama, north of Kyoto. It is said to be where Ushiwakamaru (Minamoto no Yoshitsune) trained as a child, and it is known for legends of tengu (long-nosed mountain goblins) living in the mountains. The approach from the Nio Gate to the main hall is a deep mountain path through cedar groves, and a cable car is also available. Hiking over the mountain to Kibune is popular as well.
quiz_en: What was the childhood name of the warrior who is said to have trained on Mount Kurama as a boy and learned swordsmanship from tengu?

desc_en: This Zen temple began as a mountain villa built by Ashikaga Yoshimasa, the eighth shogun of the Muromachi shogunate. Its Kannon hall, the Ginkaku, has a quiet presence that conveys the beauty of wabi-sabi. Highlights include the Ginshadan, white sand raked into wave patterns, the cone-shaped Kogetsudai, and the moss-covered stroll garden, where you can feel the essence of Higashiyama culture.
quiz_en: What is the sculpture of white sand heaped into the shape of a truncated cone in the garden of Ginkaku-ji called?

desc_en: Founded in the Meiji era to commemorate the 1,100th anniversary of the transfer of the capital to Heian-kyo, this shrine honors Emperor Kanmu, who established Heian-kyo, and others. The vermilion buildings are a scaled-down reproduction of the main hall of state of the Heian-kyo palace, and the great torii (shrine gate) of Okazaki is also a Kyoto landmark. In the shrine garden surrounding the buildings, red weeping cherry trees in spring and irises in early summer bloom beautifully.
quiz_en: Which emperor, who moved the capital to Heian-kyo, is enshrined at Heian Jingu Shrine in Kyoto?

desc_en: This temple in Iwakura, Sakyo Ward, Kyoto, was founded on the site of Emperor Go-Mizunoo's mountain villa, the Hataeda Palace. The view of Mount Hiei beyond the dry landscape garden of stones set in moss is just like a painting. Known as one of Kyoto's finest borrowed-scenery gardens, it uses a hedge and cedar trees to frame Mount Hiei like a picture frame.
quiz_en: What is the garden technique, as seen at Entsu-ji, of incorporating a distant mountain into the garden's scenery called?

desc_en: This mountain villa at the foot of Mount Hiei was built by Retired Emperor Go-Mizunoo in the early Edo period. It consists of three villas, the upper, middle and lower, with fields spreading between them, and this peaceful scenery is part of its charm. From the heights of the upper villa, a grand view extends over Yokuryuchi Pond and the streets of Kyoto, as far as the western hills. A visit requires an application to the Imperial Household Agency.
quiz_en: Which early Edo-period retired emperor built the Shugakuin Imperial Villa at the foot of Mount Hiei?

desc_en: Built by Tokugawa Ieyasu as his residence in Kyoto, this castle witnessed both the beginning and the end of the Edo shogunate. The Ninomaru Palace is designated a National Treasure as an example of Edo-period palace architecture and is known for its corridors that make a sound like birdsong when walked on. In 1867, the fifteenth shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu announced the return of political power to the emperor here.
quiz_en: What are the corridors in the Ninomaru Palace of Nijo Castle that make a sound like birdsong when you walk on them called?

desc_en: This old temple stands halfway up Mount Otowa in the Higashiyama hills and is known for the "Stage of Kiyomizu" jutting out over a cliff. The main hall's stage is built in the kakezukuri style without using nails, and in cherry blossom and autumn leaf seasons the view below becomes a sea of flowers or foliage. The Otowa Waterfall on the grounds and the bustling Kiyomizu-zaka approach are also classic Kyoto sightseeing.
quiz_en: What is the architectural style, as in Kiyomizu-dera's main hall, of supporting a floor with long pillars set on a cliff called?

desc_en: This temple in Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, is known for its hall stretching long from north to south. It is called Sanjusangendo because the main hall has 33 bays between its pillars, and inside, 1,001 statues of the Thousand-Armed Kannon stand in rows in an overwhelming sight. In the Edo period, the toshiya archery contest, in which archers competed in skill, was held under the eaves of the main hall.
quiz_en: How many statues of the Thousand-Armed Kannon stand in rows inside the hall of Sanjusangendo in total?

desc_en: This head temple of the Tofuku-ji branch of Rinzai Zen in Higashiyama Ward is one of Kyoto's finest autumn foliage spots. The leaves seen from the Tsutenkyo Bridge spanning the ravine look like a sea of red clouds filling the valley. Don't miss the National Treasure Sanmon gate, among the oldest surviving Zen temple gates, and the Hojo gardens known for their checkerboard-patterned moss garden.
quiz_en: At Tofuku-ji, which covered bridge is known for its view down into the ravine dyed with autumn leaves?

desc_en: Located in Gion, Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, this shrine is affectionately known as "Gion-san". It enshrines Susanoo and other deities, and the Gion Matsuri in July is this shrine's festival. The vermilion West Tower Gate at the end of Shijo-dori is the symbol of Gion, and at night the dance hall lit with lanterns creates a magical atmosphere.
quiz_en: Which deity, the main deity of Yasaka Shrine, is known for slaying the eight-headed serpent Yamata no Orochi?

desc_en: Spreading in front of Yasaka Shrine, this is Kyoto's signature hanamachi (geisha district). Lattice-fronted machiya townhouses and teahouses line Hanamikoji, and at dusk you may glimpse a graceful maiko. The willow-lined Shirakawa canal and stone-paved lanes are also full of quiet charm, and simply walking here lets you fully savor the essence of Kyoto.
quiz_en: What are the young women seen in Gion who are training to become geiko (Kyoto geisha) called?

desc_en: This sloping stone-stepped approach leads to Kiyomizu-dera and is also called "Sannenzaka". Traditional machiya townhouses line the slope, with shops selling Kyo-yaki pottery, Japanese sweets, pickles and more. The area continuing from Ninenzaka to the Yasaka Pagoda has been selected as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings, offering a stroll steeped in the atmosphere of the old capital.
quiz_en: According to the folk saying told about Sanneizaka, someone who trips on the slope will die within how many years?

desc_en: This national museum in Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, collects and exhibits paintings, sculptures, crafts and more, centered on Kyoto's cultural properties from the Heian through the Edo periods. The brick Meiji Kotokan building, built in the Meiji era, is an Important Cultural Property, distinguished by the elegance of Western-style architecture. The museum stands across from Sanjusangendo.
quiz_en: Which architect, who also designed the Akasaka Palace, designed the Meiji Kotokan building of the Kyoto National Museum?

desc_en: Standing at the east end of Shijo Ohashi Bridge, the Minamiza is said to have the oldest history of any theater in Japan. Beloved as a temple of kabuki since the Edo period, its annual December "Kichirei Kaomise Kogyo" is a year-end tradition in Kyoto. During the run, signboards bearing the actors' names in the Kanteiryu style of lettering are displayed on the front of the theater, making the town festive.
quiz_en: What are the signboards bearing the actors' names, displayed on the front of the Minamiza during the Kaomise performances, called?

desc_en: This spring dance performance, featuring all the geiko and maiko of Gion Kobu, has continued since the Meiji era. Geiko and maiko in splendid costumes perform dances in unison, with each scene depicting seasonal views. The curtain-raising cries of "Miyako Odori wa" and "Yoiyasa" are another famous feature of this traditional event that colors spring in Kyoto.
quiz_en: At the opening of the Miyako Odori, what call do the geiko and maiko answer with after the cry of "Miyako Odori wa"?

desc_en: Located north of Kyoto Station, this head temple of the Shinshu Otani school is affectionately known as "Ohigashi-san". The Goeido (Founder's Hall), which enshrines the image of the founder Shinran, is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world, and its size is overwhelming. Shoseien (Kikokutei), on a detached part of the grounds, is known as a beautiful pond-stroll garden.
quiz_en: Who is the founder of Jodo Shinshu Buddhism whose image is enshrined in the Founder's Hall of Higashi Hongan-ji?

desc_en: This head temple of the Hongwanji school of Jodo Shinshu in Shimogyo Ward is affectionately known as "Onishi-san". Registered as a World Cultural Heritage site, it has the National Treasure Goeido and Amida Hall, and the Karamon gate adorned with gorgeous carvings. The shoin halls and Hiunkaku pavilion, which convey Momoyama culture, are also National Treasures, and the magnificent temple complex is overwhelming.
quiz_en: Because it is so beautiful you never tire of looking at it, what is the Karamon gate of Nishi Hongan-ji also called?

desc_en: Built when Heian-kyo was founded and later entrusted to Kobo Daishi Kukai, this is the fundamental training center of Shingon Buddhism. Its five-story pagoda, about 55 meters tall, is the tallest wooden tower in Japan and a symbol of Kyoto. The three-dimensional mandala in the Lecture Hall is breathtaking, and the "Kobo-ichi" market held on the 21st of every month draws large crowds.
quiz_en: Which monk was entrusted with To-ji by Emperor Saga and made it the fundamental training center of Shingon esoteric Buddhism?

desc_en: This temple of the Myoshin-ji branch of Rinzai Zen in Ukyo Ward is world famous for its rock garden of 15 stones set in white sand. It is said that from wherever you look, you cannot see all the stones at once, and its appeal is a simple beauty left to the viewer's imagination. The stroll garden around Kyoyochi Pond also shows beautiful scenery in every season.
quiz_en: How many stones in total are placed in the famous white-sand rock garden of Ryoan-ji Temple?

desc_en: Located in Arashiyama, this head temple of the Tenryu-ji branch of Rinzai Zen was founded by Ashikaga Takauji to pray for the repose of Emperor Go-Daigo. The Sogenchi Garden, designed by Muso Soseki, is a grand pond-stroll garden borrowing the scenery of Arashiyama and Mount Kameyama, and it was the first in Japan designated a Historic Site and Special Place of Scenic Beauty. Beyond the north gate, the bamboo grove path continues.
quiz_en: Which Zen monk designed the Sogenchi Garden of Tenryu-ji and also became the temple's first head priest?

desc_en: Located in Hanazono, Ukyo Ward, Kyoto, this head temple of the Myoshin-ji branch of Rinzai Zen is a great Zen temple with many sub-temples lining its vast grounds. On the ceiling of the Lecture Hall is a painting of a dragon in clouds whose expression is said to change depending on where you stand. You can also enjoy famous gardens, each with a different character, at sub-temples such as Taizo-in and Keishun-in.
quiz_en: Which Edo-period painter created the cloud dragon painting on the ceiling of the Lecture Hall at Myoshin-ji?

desc_en: Located in Uzumasa, Ukyo Ward, Kyoto, this theme park is attached to a studio for jidaigeki (period dramas). Open-air sets spread out, including Edo-period streets, Yoshiwara and Meiji-era townscapes, and actual filming sometimes takes place. With attractions such as ninja shows and period costume experiences, you can step into the world of the movies.
quiz_en: If you dressed up in period costume at Toei Kyoto Studio Park, would you want to be a samurai, a townswoman or a ninja?

desc_en: Spreading across Mount Daigo in Fushimi Ward, Kyoto, this is the head temple of the Daigo school of Shingon Buddhism. It is a famous cherry blossom spot where Toyotomi Hideyoshi held the lavish "Daigo Flower Viewing" late in life, and in spring the grounds are wrapped in blossoms. The five-story pagoda, built in the Heian period, is designated a National Treasure as the oldest wooden building in Kyoto Prefecture. It is a component of the World Cultural Heritage site.
quiz_en: What is the lavish flower-viewing party that Toyotomi Hideyoshi held at Daigo-ji late in his life called?

desc_en: This Rinzai Zen temple in Nishikyo Ward, Kyoto, is called "Koke-dera" (Moss Temple) for the beauty of the moss covering its grounds. Many kinds of moss grow in the garden designed by Muso Soseki, and a green carpet surrounds Ogonchi Pond. Visits require advance application, and visitors proceed to the garden after religious practices such as sutra copying.
quiz_en: Which Zen monk designed the garden that gave Saiho-ji Temple its popular nickname, the "Moss Temple"?

desc_en: Built on the banks of the Katsura River in the early Edo period as a villa for the Hachijo-no-miya family, this is an imperial villa. Its stroll garden, centered on a pond with teahouses and shoin halls, is considered a masterpiece of Japanese gardens, and it is also known for the high praise of German architect Bruno Taut. Visits require an application to the Imperial Household Agency and are guided tours.
quiz_en: Which German architect lavishly praised the simple beauty of the Katsura Imperial Villa in Kyoto?

desc_en: This old temple in Kannonji, Fukuchiyama, is affectionately known as the "Hydrangea Temple of Tanba". In the rainy season, many hydrangeas bloom across the grounds, with blue, purple and white flowers enveloping the stone steps and halls. Hydrangeas wet with rain are even more vivid, letting you savor the gentle mood of early summer.
quiz_en: At Kannon-ji, known as the "Hydrangea Temple of Tanba", which color of hydrangea do you like best?

desc_en: This autumn festival is held at Nukata Ichinomiya Shrine in Fukuchiyama. Fukuchiyama is a castle town in Tanba through which the Yura River flows, and in the surrounding villages, festivals giving thanks for an abundant harvest in autumn have been handed down. On festival day, mikoshi (portable shrines) and drums go around the area, and lively shouts echo through the mountain village.
quiz_en: At the Nukata Ichinomiya Shrine autumn festival, what kind of moment do you think would make your heart race the most?

desc_en: This park on a hill in Kisaichi, Ayabe, preserves one of the largest round burial mounds in Kyoto Prefecture. The tomb's covering stones and haniwa clay figures have been restored, recreating its appearance at the time it was built. From the top of the mound you can look over the Yura River, the streets of Ayabe and the surrounding mountains, and imagine the ancient clans who ruled this land.
quiz_en: What is a kofun burial mound that looks round when seen from above, like Kisaichi Maruyama Kofun, called?

desc_en: This sandbar stretches about 3.6 kilometers across Miyazu Bay. A row of pine trees, said to number about 8,000, lines it, and it is counted among the Three Views of Japan along with Matsushima and Miyajima. When viewed upside down between your legs from Kasamatsu Park or Amanohashidate View Land, a practice called "matanozoki", it is said to look like a bridge spanning the heavens.
quiz_en: What is the way of viewing Amanohashidate by bending over backward-facing on a hilltop and looking between your legs called?

desc_en: This Hachiman shrine stands in Shino, Kameoka. It is known as the place where Ashikaga Takauji raised troops to overthrow the shogunate at the end of the Kamakura period, and the associated Hatatate-yanagi (flag-raising willow) remains on the grounds. Located at a key point linking Tanba and Kyoto, it was the stage for a turning point in history. In the tree-surrounded grounds, you can imagine those days.
quiz_en: Which warrior raised troops at Shinomura Hachimangu Shrine in Kameoka to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate?

desc_en: Located in Chitose, Kameoka, this ancient shrine is the Ichinomiya (highest-ranking shrine) of Tanba Province and reveres Mount Mikage behind it as its sacred body. It draws faith as a shrine of matchmaking, and on its grounds traces of ancient nature worship remain, such as iwakura (sacred rocks) and spring water. The main hall is designated an Important Cultural Property, and pure air fills the quiet forest.
quiz_en: Izumo Daijingu in Kameoka has been revered as the Ichinomiya of which old province in central Kyoto Prefecture?

desc_en: This waterfall lies in the hills of eastern Joyo. Joyo is located midway between Kyoto and Nara and is also known for plum blossom spots such as the Aodani Plum Grove. The waterfall, cascading down a quiet stream surrounded by trees, has a charm hard to believe so close to town, and it is a place to feel cool air during a walk.
quiz_en: If you visited Kamodani Falls, which other sights or local specialties would you like to enjoy in Joyo City?

desc_en: This is the annual grand festival of Muko Shrine, which stands on Mukoyama in Muko City. Muko Shrine is an ancient shrine with a long approach, and its main hall, built in the Muromachi period, is designated an Important Cultural Property. In spring the approach is wrapped in cherry blossoms, and in the grounds, beautiful with autumn leaves, you can enjoy the liveliness of a festival handed down by local people.
quiz_en: If you visited the annual grand festival of Muko Shrine, what would you like to see while walking along the approach?

desc_en: This shrine in Nagaokakyo honors Sugawara no Michizane. Along both sides of the approach crossing Hachijogaike Pond on the grounds, old Kirishima azaleas are planted, and in spring they burst into flaming crimson bloom. The shrine is said to have originated when Michizane stopped here and lamented his parting on his way into exile in Dazaifu.
quiz_en: Which azalea variety colors the approach across Hachijogaike Pond at Nagaoka Tenmangu a deep crimson in spring?

desc_en: This park in Nagaokakyo preserves the site of Shoryuji Castle. In the Sengoku period, Hosokawa Fujitaka was lord of the castle, and Akechi Mitsuhide's daughter Tama (later Hosokawa Gracia) is said to have married Hosokawa Tadaoki here. During the Battle of Yamazaki, Mitsuhide used it as his base. With restored moats, stone walls and a replica turret, it is pleasant for a stroll.
quiz_en: By what name is the daughter of Akechi Mitsuhide, said to have married Hosokawa Tadaoki at Shoryuji Castle, known?

desc_en: This ancient shrine, founded in the Heian period, stands atop Mount Otoko in Yawata. As the shrine guarding Kyoto's ura-kimon (the unlucky southwest direction), it received deep reverence from the imperial court and samurai, and its main hall is designated a National Treasure. You can ride a cable car to the top, and from the observation deck you can see all of central Kyoto. A monument associated with Edison stands on the grounds.
quiz_en: Who invented the light bulb whose filament used bamboo from the area around Iwashimizu Hachimangu?

desc_en: This plateau spreads over the hills of Tango, Kyotango City. It is an open tableland near the Sea of Japan with ranches and farms, where you can see cattle leisurely grazing. From the heights you can see the horizon of the Sea of Japan, and at dusk the sun sinking into the sea creates a beautiful scene. It is a perfect detour on a drive around the Tango Peninsula.
quiz_en: After gazing at the Sea of Japan from the Ikari Plateau, which Tango Peninsula sight would you like to visit next?

desc_en: Spreading in the north of Miyama, Nantan City, this village preserves many farmhouses with thatched roofs and is called "Kayabuki no Sato" (Village of Thatched Roofs). It has been selected as a national Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings, and Japan's traditional rural landscape spreads through the hills along the Yura River. The simultaneous water cannon spraying in spring and autumn, and the snowy scenery in winter, also enchant many visitors.
quiz_en: At the Miyama thatched-roof village, what is the event in which water cannons spray water all at once as a fire equipment check called?
